title: 实现本地账号生命周期核心与口令风险门禁
changed_contracts: Adds the internal GatewayAuth administrator-authorized local-account lifecycle, mandatory fail-closed secret-risk port and stable lifecycle result contract; no public wire contract or HTTP route changed.
Adds production migration 11 for idempotent no-secret account lifecycle state and bounded privileged functions, advancing exact embedded database readiness from 10 to 11.
risks: No production common/breached-secret checker is implemented, so production provisioning remains intentionally unavailable and must not be replaced with direct SQL.
First-administrator bootstrap, out-of-band recovery and deployment authorization secrets are not implemented; without an authenticated administrator every lifecycle command fails closed.

The current Host remains HTTP-only and exposes no login or account-management route. TLS, secure cookies, Origin/CSRF enforcement, persistent keys and upstream abuse control must precede any endpoint mapping.
Database actor identifiers and session versions must come only from the V01-011 authenticated session boundary; future adapters must never accept client-asserted actor identity.
GitHub-hosted Linux CI was not executed in this thread; workflow and source policy were validated locally against Windows and PostgreSQL 16.15.

architecture_review.module: GatewayAuth local account lifecycle application service and PostgreSQL adapter
reused_existing_logic: Reuses V01-011 AuthenticatedIdentity, LocalAccountName, LocalSecret, PBKDF2 policy, credential/session version semantics and authenticated_principal as the only administrator fact source.
Reuses the existing PostgreSQL authentication executor, fixed owner/runtime roles, SECURITY DEFINER pattern, migration manifest, backup-before-apply flow and PostgreSQL 16.15 verification.
Reuses one sensitive credential hash-material implementation for both login reads and new credential enrollment, including validation, disposal and zeroization.
Reuses the centrally locked Npgsql 10.0.3 dependency and existing CoreServer modular-monolith assembly; no package, framework, language, database or host was added.
cross_module_access: All new persistent state and functions remain inside gateway_auth and are owned by assetlibrary_gateway_auth_owner.
The gateway-auth runtime role has no direct lifecycle-table access and cannot execute the internal actor helper; it receives only four bounded function grants.
Application and Contracts contain no Npgsql, ASP.NET, filesystem, network or operating-system dependency; Infrastructure implements the lifecycle store.
No LibraryStorage or other module table, internal entity or mutable state is read or written.
contract_changes: Adds internal lifecycle outcomes and state plus a mandatory secret-risk port without changing contracts/** or generated SDKs.
Adds append-only migration 11; migrations 1 through 10, roles.sql, bootstrap.sql and the fixed 26-role graph remain unchanged.
Advances CoreServer database readiness to the exact eleven-migration ledger while preserving fail-closed pending, extra and drift outcomes.
architecture_tests: Locked restore, format/analyzer verification, zero-warning Release build and all 220 .NET tests passed; GatewayAuth WebGateway is 36/36 and Packaging is 30/30.

All 62 database tests passed against a real disposable PostgreSQL 16.15 server, including administrator revalidation, idempotency, session invalidation, recovery persistence, restart and last-administrator concurrency.
54 repository, 14 architecture and 32 release tests passed; migration, .NET source, repository, server-release and Alpha integration validators passed.
v0.1-start remains allowed, while Alpha --require-ready and v0.1-release retain native exit code 3 with production authentication and all prior release blockers intact.
technical_debt: Implement a production common/breached-secret checker with bounded privacy-preserving requests, caching and an explicit unavailable state.
Implement first-administrator bootstrap and out-of-band recovery with deployment authorization, audit and rotation before an account-management adapter exists.
Compose authentication into the shared Host only after TLS, persistent keys, secure cookies, Origin/CSRF and upstream abuse-control boundaries are complete.
Keep business APIs and every production file-write path disabled until their existing integration and durability gates close.
